proposals.name: Foreground microlens on red source
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point mass is slowly transiting a red background source, so its achromatic magnification keeps both bands rising together at nearly constant g-r colour for over 60 days. This long, accelerating, colour-stable rise is not a Type Ia approaching a normal peak and decline, but a lensing approach toward maximum magnification.
proposals.predicts: It predicts both bands peak together after now and then fall symmetrically at essentially constant g-r colour, returning to the faint baseline, unlike a Type Ia that should already be fading and reddening.

proposals.name: Galactic microlensing of red star
proposals.idea: At this low Galactic latitude a foreground point lens is slowly magnifying a background red giant, producing a months-long rise far slower than a supernova. A constant component accounts for blended, unlensed light in each band.
proposals.predicts: Both bands will keep rising together with nearly unchanged g-r colour to one peak, then decline symmetrically to the pre-event baseline, unlike a Type Ia whose colour evolves and which fades irreversibly after maximum.

proposals.name: Drifting subtraction residual leak
proposals.idea: In this crowded low Galactic latitude field, a mis-registered or seeing-mismatched template leaves a residual from a nearby bright red star at the transient position. A slow seasonal drift in alignment or calibration makes that residual grow steadily and redly, mimicking a still-rising supernova while intermittent well-matched epochs subtract cleanly to about 20.8 mag limits.
proposals.predicts: It predicts future flux rises linearly at the same per-band rate with unchanged roughly 1.5 mag g-r offset, centroid and stamp residuals tied to the neighbour, and occasional deep non-detections on well-matched epochs, rather than peaking and fading as the Ia model requires.

proposals.name: Galactic microlensing alignment
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point lens in the Galactic plane is gradually aligning with a red background source, achromatically magnifying it on top of its steady baseline light. This replaces the Ia explosion, explaining the >60-day monotonic rise at nearly constant r-g colour that the Ia fit mistook for a post-peak decline.
proposals.predicts: It predicts an achromatic symmetric turnover and fall back to the pre-rise constant baseline at unchanged r-g colour, rather than an Ia-like reddening radioactive decline.

proposals.name: Galactic point microlensing
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point mass in the Galactic plane is magnifying a distant, intrinsically red background star, producing the slow brightening seen for over 60 days. Both bands rise together by about 1.7 mag at an almost constant g-r colour of roughly 1.5 mag, as expected for achromatic lensing rather than an expanding, cooling supernova.
proposals.predicts: It predicts an achromatic turnover followed by a symmetric decline on the same timescale back to the constant pre-event baseline at unchanged colour, unlike a Type Ia supernova which should redden, develop evolving spectral features, and fade irreversibly after peak.
